summary: Interpreted the executed restore-on-monotonic-store experiment (CheckRun b78bcab64b0d41b5adaafa98cc0c7f43, exit 0, tests_passed) as a negative result that narrows the earlier source-only hypothesis. Parsed index 1: the production Restore completed with a nil error, the snapshot index moved to 104 and the applied index to 105, but the store's last index was also 105, so store_emptied=false and should_snapshot stayed false; parsed index 2, after more than four snapshot intervals, shows the verdict still false with the stored-snapshot count unchanged at 2, so no repeated snapshot was created. The mechanism that defeats the premise is that removeOldLogs does clear the store during the restore, but the Restore API then appends a trailing noop entry and waits for it, leaving one entry above the snapshot index and a small positive delta instead of an underflow. Recorded as violated with defect_claim refuted for this producer, explicitly noting the asserted snapshot-trigger defect is untouched (it rests on its own TrailingLogs=0 witness) and that its limitations now include the user-restore path not being an additional producer under these conditions, with the snapshot-install variant still unexercised.
